# Odyn Gateway operational dashboard
Shows route-level request volume and latency, upstream dependency outcomes, token usage, and accounting events. Prompts, completions, bearer tokens, provider credentials, and raw identity claims are not collected.

content.query: requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "gateway.chat" | extend Route=coalesce(tostring(customDimensions["http.route"]), name) | summarize Requests=sum(itemCount), Errors=sumif(itemCount, toint(resultCode) >= 500), Throttles=sumif(itemCount, resultCode == "429"), AuthFailures=sumif(itemCount, resultCode in ("401", "403")) by Route, bin(timestamp, 1m) | render timechart
content.title: Request rate and errors

content.query: requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "gateway.chat" | extend Route=coalesce(tostring(customDimensions["http.route"]), name) | summarize P50=percentile(duration, 50), P95=percentile(duration, 95), P99=percentile(duration, 99) by Route, bin(timestamp, 1m) | render timechart
content.title: Latency percentiles

content.query: dependencies | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "POST" and target == "POST" | summarize Calls=sum(itemCount), Failures=sumif(itemCount, success == false), P95=percentile(duration, 95) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | render timechart
content.title: OpenRouter provider dependency outcomes

content.query: customMetrics | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "gateway.events" | extend Event=tostring(customDimensions.event) | summarize Events=sum(valueSum) by Event | order by Events desc
content.title: Security and accounting events

content.query: customMetrics | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "gateway.upstream.requests" | summarize Requests=sum(valueSum) by tostring(customDimensions.outcome), bin(timestamp, 1m) | render timechart
content.title: Upstream request outcomes (requests)

content.query: customMetrics | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "gateway.upstream.duration" | summarize DurationSeconds=sum(valueSum), Samples=sum(valueCount) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | extend MeanSeconds=iff(Samples > 0, DurationSeconds/Samples, real(null)) | project timestamp, MeanSeconds | render timechart
content.title: Upstream latency (seconds)

content.query: customMetrics | where timestamp > ago(1h) and name == "gateway.tokens" | summarize Tokens=sum(valueSum) by tostring(customDimensions.model), tostring(customDimensions.direction), bin(timestamp, 1m) | render timechart
content.title: Token usage (tokens)

content.json:
# Alert response runbooks

Azure Monitor alert conditions distinguish `monitorCondition` (Fired/Resolved) from `state` (user acknowledgement). Use the linked operational runbooks for response steps. Notification actions must be configured for each environment.

---

# Runbook: gateway errors and latency

1. Identify the affected route, region and running application revision.
2. Correlate gateway request/dependency telemetry using request and trace IDs.
   Do not include prompts, responses, bearer tokens or credentials in incident
   notes.
3. Separate gateway 502/503/504 responses, shared-store errors, upstream
   failures and readiness/revision failures.
   For a 502 with the allowlisted reason `no_text_token_limit`, check whether
   model reasoning consumed the configured output cap before visible text was
   produced. The gateway disables reasoning for chat completions; verify the
   active revision uses the expected image digest before changing token limits.
   Do not log or expose reasoning content.
4. Pause synthetic traffic when the authoritative store is unhealthy. Do not
   automatically replay a provider request if the provider may already have
   processed it.
5. For a confirmed bad revision, roll back to a known-good image digest using
   the deployment procedure. Verify health and a bounded request after
   mitigation.

---

# Runbook: authentication failures

1. Separate 401 responses (missing/invalid authentication) from 403 responses
   (valid identity without the required permission).
2. Compare the time window with identity-provider, key-rotation and gateway
   configuration changes.
3. Inspect aggregate status and redacted diagnostics only. Never record raw
   access tokens or personal token claims.
4. Verify issuer, audience, signing-key refresh and the expected delegated
   scope or application role. Do not weaken token validation to restore access.
5. After mitigation, test one valid human flow and one valid workload flow,
   then confirm invalid tokens still fail closed.

---

# Runbook: throttling responses

1. Compare aggregate 429 responses with the configured per-principal/global
   rate and budget limits.
2. Confirm responses include a valid integer `Retry-After` and clients back off
   instead of retrying in a tight loop.
3. Check shared-store health, admission latency and conditional-write conflicts.
   Distinguish intentional rejection from storage failures reported as 503.
4. If a client is looping or the store is unhealthy, reduce or pause its
   traffic. Do not relax admission limits during an incident without reviewing
   the capacity and cost impact.
5. After mitigation, verify a valid request succeeds and rejected requests
   still receive bounded retry guidance.

---

# Runbook: accounting and shared-store anomalies

1. Correlate safe request IDs and trace IDs; inspect aggregate reservation,
   usage and store events. Never log prompts, credentials or bearer tokens.
2. Keep admission fail-closed while the authoritative store is unavailable. Do
   not fall back to process-local accounting.
3. Preserve conservative reservations when provider usage is unknown. Do not
   release a reservation or replay an ambiguous paid request automatically.
4. Check model pricing configuration, request caps, transaction conflicts and
   store latency. Pause live traffic if accounting correctness is uncertain.
5. Reconcile provider usage through approved private tooling before correcting
   an account. Verify recovery with controlled stub requests before resuming
   live traffic.

---

# Runbook: shared-store contention

1. Reduce or stop load while investigating. Do not rerun a failing stress test
   against a live provider.
2. Compare aggregate response counts with gateway admission-conflict events and
   storage transaction diagnostics. Inspect transaction sub-operation outcomes,
   not only the outer batch response.
3. Confirm active image digest, replica count, request deadlines and shared
   store health. A process-local coordinator can reduce same-process stampedes;
   the store remains the cross-replica authority.
4. Keep admission fail-closed. Do not switch to in-memory state or retry a
   provider request whose dispatch status is ambiguous.
5. Recovery requires intentional throttling to return 429 with valid
   `Retry-After`, storage-induced 503s to stop, and reservations to remain
   atomic under concurrent writers.
